official.description_text:
Doctoral student (licentiate) in digital twins for electrified construction
Apply for position
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Architecture and Built Environment
Project description
Third-cycle subject: Geodesy and Geoinformatics, with specialisation in Geoinformatics
We are seeking a doctoral student for a two-year licentiate position in
DISSECT
, which develops data-driven models and decision support for emission-free, resource-efficient and electrified construction.
The doctoral student will work with DISSECT’s material and logistics layers. The research may include GeoBIM and 3D voxel models of ground conditions, quantities and material flows; material tracking; volume and mass estimation; inverse geological modelling; and analysis of sensor and telematics data from machines and transports. The logistics part may include optimization of construction processes, mass transports, circular material flows and charging constraints.
Methodologically, the work may combine geospatial data management, database technology, data science, machine learning, simulation and optimization, including model predictive control and reinforcement learning. The aim is digital-twin-based decision support for electrified groundwork construction.
The position is placed at the Division of Geoinformatics, KTH, and linked to ITRL and the DISSECT consortium. The initial goal is a licentiate degree after two years, but the research and doctoral studies are planned to continue toward a doctoral degree, subject to continued funding and formal decisions.
Supervision:
Associate Professor Gyözö Gidofalvi is proposed to supervise the doctoral student. Professor Jonas Mårtensson is proposed as co-supervisor. Decisions are made on admission
Admission requirements
To be admitted to postgraduate education (Chapter 7, 39 § Swedish Higher Education Ordinance), the applicant must have basic eligibility in accordance with either of the following:
passed a second cycle degree (for example a master's degree), or
completed course requirements of at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 second-cycle higher education credits, or
acquired, in some other way within or outside the country, substantially equivalent knowledge
In addition to the above, there is also a
mandatory requirement for English equivalent to English B/6.
Selection
In order to succeed as a doctoral student at KTH you need to be goal oriented and persevering in your work. During the selection process, candidates will be assessed upon their ability to:
independently pursue his or her work
collaborate with others,
have a professional approach and
analyze and work with complex issues.
Preferred qualifications are:
Experience with simulation, optimization, or digital twin systems,
Experience with cloud environments and containerized applications,
Experience handling large datasets,
Interest in energy systems and sustainability.
Experience from research or industry projects.
Good communication skills in both English and Swedish, as they are required in day-to-day work.
After the qualification requirements, great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Target degree: Licentiate degree
Information regarding admission and employment
Only those admitted to postgraduate education may be employed as a doctoral student. The total length of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education in four years' time. An employed doctoral student can, to a limited extent (maximum 20%), perform certain tasks within their role, e.g. training and administration. A new position as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, and then the employment may be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time. In the case of studies that are to be completed with a licentiate degree, the total period of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education for two years.
As a doctoral student, you are entitled to a workplace with
many employee benefits
and monthly salary according to
KTH’s Doctoral student salary agreement
. Read more about

.

To apply for the position
Apply for the position and admission through KTH's recruitment system. It is the applicant’s responsibility to ensure that the application is complete in accordance with the instructions in the advertisement.
Applications must include the following elements:
Copies of diplomas and grades from previous university studies and certificates of fulfilled
language requirements (see above)
. Translations into English or Swedish if the original document is not issued in one of these languages.Copies of originals must be
certified
.

Application letter with a brief description of why you want to pursue research studies, about what your academic interests are and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. (Maximum 2 pages long)
Representative publications or technical reports. For longer documents, please provide a summary (abstract) and a web link to the full text.
Applications must be received at the last closing date at midnight, CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).

In such cases, a prerequisite for employment is that the applicant is approved following the security clearance.
We firmly decline all contact with staffing and recruitment agencies and job ad salespersons.

ai.summary: Two-year licentiate position in digital twins for electrified construction, focusing on GeoBIM, 3D voxel modelling, material tracking, logistics optimization, and machine-learning-based decision support. Emphasizes data science, simulation, and optimization rather than human interaction.

thematic_fit.rationale: Position involves digital twins—a concept present in researcher's Master's work (campus digital twin). However, the application domain (construction logistics and material flows) and outcomes (process optimization, resource efficiency) are entirely different from spatial learning and wayfinding. The XR/visualization layer is absent; focus is data-driven optimization. Thematic overlap is superficial.

methodological_fit.rationale: Both involve digital twin design and simulation. Researcher has experience building XR-based digital twins with collaborative, user-centred evaluation. This position emphasizes data management, ML, optimization, and simulation—methodologically adjacent but not aligned. Researcher could learn simulation and optimization methods, but the human-centred user study approach is not the primary focus here. Moderate methodological bridge exists via shared digital-twin systems thinking.

growth_value.rationale: Position would develop skills in simulation, optimization, data management, and machine learning—useful capabilities for future digital-twin and immersive-systems research. However, these are instrumental skills (ML, optimization) rather than core human-centred research capabilities (spatial cognition, user evaluation, collaborative interaction design). Closes some gaps (data science, simulation) but not primary ones (spatial learning outcomes, human factors).

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is excellent; funding (DISSECT consortium, ITRL) is stable and substantial. However, supervisor (Gidofalvi) and group focus (geoinformatics, logistics optimization, data science) are not HCI or immersive systems. Position would develop technical skills in a domain (construction/sustainability) that does not align with researcher's stated target identity. Licentiate duration (2 years) is shorter than full PhD, which may limit depth.

eligibility_flags: Posting states 'preferred qualifications' for simulation, optimization, cloud environments, and large-dataset handling; researcher has none of these at advanced level.
Position is licentiate (2 years) rather than full PhD; researcher's target is PhD-level trajectory.
Swedish language strongly preferred for day-to-day work; researcher's proficiency unknown.
Security clearance may apply; ambiguous in posting.
risks: Digital twin is shared concept, but application domain (construction logistics) is distant from spatial learning and wayfinding.
Heavy focus on ML optimization and data science; researcher would need to ramp up quickly on unfamiliar algorithms and tools.
Supervisor's background (geoinformatics, optimization) is not HCI or human-centred systems research.
Licentiate (2 years) is shorter degree; may leave gaps for full doctoral-level research contributions.
PhD trajectory would shift toward data-driven optimization rather than human-centred immersive systems.
Sustainability/construction domain does not align with researcher's spatial learning and wayfinding focus.
